conceptZh: 科學家老鼠與牠的影子小鼠互相模仿，兩人往外撐開成八。
object: a bespectacled lab mouse and a tiny copycat mouse beside bubbling beakers
morph: two mice leaning outward in mirror poses become the strokes of 八
creativeAngle: 跟屁蟲：小鼠慢一拍模仿科學家，兩條腿誤打誤撞岔開；八字鬍是最後的笑點，鬍子畫成八字形。
promptEn:
An 8-second clip on a soft lilac lab backdrop with pale sky-blue counters and green bubbling beakers. A bespectacled cartoon lab mouse in a white coat faces a tiny copycat mouse that mimics each motion one beat late. The off-screen voice, warm and clear Taiwanese Mandarin, says exactly: 「八、八、八字鬍」 (ㄅㄚ、ㄅㄚ、ㄅㄚ ㄗˋ ㄏㄨˊ), slowly with clear tones, then stops.
0.0-1.8s: The scientist raises both arms in a grand pose; the tiny mouse copies it a beat late and bumps a beaker. 「八」 (ㄅㄚ) is spoken as the first arms-up pose.
1.8-3.6s: The scientist steps back, then leans out to one side while the little mouse leans out late to the other; a fizzing beaker between them erupts a pink bubble that pushes them apart. Two thick strokes slide out like tent poles and the second 「八」 (ㄅㄚ) lands as they form a solid bright magenta glyph 八, about 70% of frame height.
3.6-5.0s: Both mice pull on matching whisker-shaped bubble moustaches that curl down in an eight-like arc; 「八字鬍」 (ㄅㄚ ㄗˋ ㄏㄨˊ) is spoken as the funny curved moustaches pop onto their faces.
5.0-8.0s: Hold: glyph 八 still and clear, centered with margins. The two mice twirl their moustaches in sync, a little late, never near the strokes.
No text except the glyph 八; no subtitles or watermark or flashing. Soft music under the voice.

conceptZh: 發條鯊魚在玩具保齡球道上先咬錯球、原地打轉，再長距離助跑、肚皮滑行撞倒橡膠恐龍排好的八個保齡球瓶；瓶子左三右五分兩邊倒成一堆，疊成八，鯊魚跳起來比全倒姿勢。
object: eight glossy tangerine toy bowling pins standing in a row at the end of a slippery toy bowling lane
morph: the belly-sliding shark crashes into the row; three pins tumble down-left and five tumble down-right, piling end to end into two diverging solid strokes that fuse into 八
creativeAngle: 與前版「老鼠互相模仿、泡泡推開」完全不同：改用肚皮滑行保齡球全倒的實體笑料，撞擊本身把八個球瓶分成左短右長兩堆疊成八，詞語「八個」正好就是畫面上八個瓶子，聽與看同一件事。鯊魚先咬錯球原地打轉是失敗一拍，恐龍用屁股扶瓶子是因為手太短，各自個性清楚。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright cartoon clip on a toy bowling lane: a glossy pale butter-yellow floor, soft mint-green walls, nothing else behind. The lead is a chunky wind-up toy shark, round belly, big goofy teeth, a silver turn-key sticking out of its back, moving with little ratchet clicks. At the far right end of the lane stand eight glossy tangerine-orange toy bowling pins in a neat row. Beside them a rubber dinosaur with enormous feet and comically tiny arms nudges the last pin upright with its hip, because its arms cannot reach. The off-screen voice, warm and clear Taiwanese Mandarin, speaks exactly these syllables, slowly and distinctly with clear tones, and nothing else: 「八、八、八個」 (ㄅㄚ、ㄅㄚ、ㄅㄚ ㄍㄜˋ). No other dialogue, no subtitles.

0.0-1.5s: The shark at the left edge stares hard at the row of pins, teeth chattering, and its key winds itself tighter with a click-click-click. The first 「八」 (ㄅㄚ) lands as the key stops and the shark lunges forward.

1.5-3.2s: Try and miss: halfway down the lane the shark snaps its jaws at the first thing it sees, a round toy bowling ball, and bites it instead. Ball jammed in its mouth, it tips onto its side and spins in a fast flat circle on the dry floor like a beached wind-up toy, eyes crossed. The dinosaur bounces its belly in a silent giggle. The shark spits the ball out; it rolls harmlessly off frame.

3.2-5.0s: The big one: the shark scoots back to the far left, key winding extra tight, a frozen half-beat of squinting anticipation, then it charges, dives onto its belly and slides across the slippery lane like a bowling ball, speed lines streaking. CRASH into the pins with a soft cartoon bonk and squash-and-stretch. The pins fly apart: three tumble down to the left, five tumble down to the right, spinning in the air and landing end to end in two tidy diagonal heaps. The heaps fuse into two thick, smooth, solid tangerine strokes: a shorter left stroke sweeping from upper center down to the lower left, and a longer right stroke sweeping from upper center down to the lower right, with a clear gap between them at the top. The second 「八」 (ㄅㄚ) is spoken exactly as the pins snap into the finished glyph 八. The dinosaur is bowled onto its back in the far right corner, huge feet in the air.

5.0-8.0s: Final hold: the glyph 八 stays perfectly still and readable, centered, about 70% of frame height with clean margins, solid tangerine on the pale yellow floor. The shark pops up in the lower-left corner in a proud strike pose, fins raised, well clear of the strokes. At about 5.3s the word 「八個」 (ㄅㄚ ㄍㄜˋ) is spoken while the eight pins embedded in the strokes each flash a tiny gleam in turn, counting along the two strokes without moving them. The shark then does one happy slow circle on the spot, and the dinosaur rocks on its back, tiny arms clapping without quite meeting.

Only text on screen is the single glyph 八. No subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing effects. Bright but not neon, no pure white blowouts, no dark grading. Soft playful music well under the voice.
